To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have identified a series of hydrophilic iminosugars, which are capable of increasing the residual glucocerebro‐sidase activity in the fibroblasts derived from Gaucher patients.

the hydrophilic active site‐specific chaperons, such as isofagomie, are less toxic to cells and are capable of increasing the residual glucocerebroside activity in fibroblast cells of Gaucher patients.

we have identified a novel class of hydrophilic small‐molecule active‐site‐ specific chaperones that increase residual glucoc erebrosidase enzyme activity in Gaucher disease‐affected cultured fibroblastic cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of small molecules as active‐site‐directed chaperones that may increase the residual glucocerebroside activity in Gaucher patients, and thus improve the clinical symptoms of the disease.
the discovery of a new class of compounds that are capable of improving the residual glucocerebro‐sidase activity of Gaucher patients by acting as active‐site‐directed chaperones.
the discovery and characterization of small molecules that can increase the activity of mutant glucoceresidase in Gaucher disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the active site‐directed chaperones are a new class of compounds with potential for the treatment of lysosomal storage disorders.

the hydrophilic iminosugars are a novel class of active‐site‐directed chaperones that have the ability to increase glucocerebrosisidase activity in Gaucher fibrobasts, which could be useful for the treatment of this disease.
the active‐site‐directed chaperones described here are a promising class of drugs for the treatment of type 1 Gaucher disease.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have found a new class of active‐site‐ specific chaperone compounds that can increase glucocerebrosis activity in Gaucher disease fibroblasts, and that these chaperones can be developed into a new drug for Gaucher disease.
we have identified a novel class of compounds with the ability to increase residual glucoceresidase activity in Gaucher fiboblasts.
the hydrophilic active site specific chaperones are capable of increasing residual enzyme activity in Gaucher fiboblasts.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the hydrophilic iminosugars, which have been used to increase the activity of lysosomal enzymes deficient in lysosomal storage disorders, are less toxic to cells than their hydrophobic counterparts.
the hydrophilic active site‐specific chaperons are less toxic to the cultured cells and are suitable candidates for drug development for the treatments of Gaucher disease.
hydrophilic small compounds, such as isofagomie, can be developed for the treatment of lysosomal storage diseases.
